incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered — pd-incident-8942 — gpu-host-evt: host gpu-node-47 unreachable (kernel panic suspected). Auto-page sent to oncall.
pagerduty: INCIDENT fired — PGD#8942 — Severity: P1 — Affected service: hosted-inference-us-west2 — routed to eng-oncall.
alex: acked. I’m on it — grabbing serial console access now.
samir: i see increased 503s on /v1/generate for a handful of customers in us-west2, spike started ~2m ago.
maria: logs show kubelet on gpu-node-47 stopped responding, nodes list shows NotReady. trying kubectl describe node gpu-node-47 now.
priya: any running Dedicated pools on that host? we have a reserved pool for acct-redwood-retail.
diego: confirmed — two pods pinned to that node: rdedicated-model-2 and eval-worker-9, both in CrashLoopBackOff on kubelet not ready.
alex: serial console attached. kernel oops backtrace visible — nvme I/O error followed by soft lockup and then kernel panic. posting snippet:
```
[ 1423.345678] nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout, aborting command
[ 1423.347890] nvidia: GPU fault detected: Xid 31
[ 1423.349012] kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
```
samir: ok — immediate mitigation plan: cordon+drain if possible, evacuate affected pods to failover zone. but first we need to stop scheduling to that rack.
maria: running `kubectl cordon gpu-node-47 && kubectl drain gpu-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — drain starting, some DaemonSets blocked (nvdriver-daemonset) because node not ready.
priya: if drain stalls due to kubelet, we may need to force delete pods and let scheduler reschedule. inform infra for host-level reset.
diego: opening infra ticket INF-2437 to request cold power cycle via BMC. assign to oncall infra.
incident-bot: PagerDuty acknowledgement: alex acknowledged PD#8942 at 2864100012.
alex: running `kubectl get pods -o wide --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-node-47` to list pinned workloads.
maria: outputs: rdedicated-model-2 (acct-redwood-retail) — NODE: gpu-node-47 — status: Unknown; eval-worker-9 — status: Pending.
samir: traffic routing — set routing rule to route new sessions away from us-west2 dedicated pool for next 15m. Maria, can you flip the failover in router-service?
maria: doing it now: `curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/v1/failover -d '{"region":"us-west2","target":"fallback-pool"}'` — response 202. monitoring.
alex: infra reports BMC access success; ipmitool console shows host unresponsive to kernel recovery; infra requests power cycle.
diego: executed `ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.0.0.47 -U admin -P **** chassis power cycle` — console went blank, host started POST.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline paused for Dedicated pool in us-west2 until node health validated.
samir: support ping: customer success notified targeted customers for potential interruption, ticket CS-6781 created and linked.
priya: are there any cached KV/corruption concerns for the models running? we should invalidate near-cache for affected model keys after node reboot.
alex: agreed — add cache invalidation job: `redis-cli -h cache-usw2 keys "model:rdedicated-model-2:*" | xargs -r redis-cli -h cache-usw2 del` after pods come back.
maria: host finished POST, kernel panics still on boot loop. BIOS shows Nvme error and firmware auto-recovery starting.
diego: infra kicking off host reprovision likely; would prefer to avoid full reprovision if drives OK. mounting remote logs and extracting dmesg to S3: `scp admin@gpu-node-47:/var/log/dmesg s3://relogs/8942/`.
alex: timeline/impact note: spike of 503s lasted ~4m, affected ~0.8% of hosted requests in us-west2 (approx 1200 requests). no payment-affecting storage writes observed.
samir: customer-impact summary to include: affected dedicated customers on that host experienced transient failures; hosted API experienced elevated 5xxs for ~4m; our fallback routing prevented wider outage.
priya: escalation: if host doesn't return healthy in 30m, we move affected Dedicated pools to reserved failover hosts and open a formal incident page.
incident-bot: Escalation scheduled at 2864102165 (30m) unless status updated.
alex: current mitigation steps done: cordon, attempted drain, BMC power cycle, failover routing engaged, support notified, infra ticket open. Next: if node fails self-recovery, schedule reprovision and migrate tenant workloads.
maria: monitoring shows traffic back to baseline after failover, error rate dropping. keeping an eye for flapping once pods reschedule.
diego: infra: NVMe SMART shows high reallocated sectors on nvme0, recommending replacing drive. filing RMA and scheduling replacement.
samir: can someone post a quick Slack blurb for #general to note brief incident and no customer data loss? I’ll draft it.
alex: i'll hand off to oncall-priya for the rest of the window — I need to jump to another page.
priya: taking over. thanks alex. I’ll keep thread updated and own the follow-ups (RMA, reprovision plan). assigning postmortem owner: maria.
maria: ack — will collect logs, timelines, and run root cause template. tagging CS-6781 for customer comms.
alex: thx. :thumbsup:
priya: one last note — ensure metric alerts set for NVMe SMART thresholds so we can preemptively replace failing drives next time.
diego: noted. INF-2437 updated with RMA ETA and replacement plan.
incident-bot: Incident PGD#8942 status: acknowledged -> in_progress. Updates will post here automatically.
deploy-bot: resumed paused pipelines in us-west2 once node count healthy.
priya: closing immediate page — will update thread when RMA scheduled and after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
pagerduty: PD#8942 acknowledged by alex (oncall) at 2864100012. Incident remains active.
